Driver's license blues

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Grace periods to renew Drivers licenses run out at the end of August but Motorists are caught up in a system that doesnt work and politicians who arent offering solutions

Unique Selling Point:
An unexpected site visit to a driving license testing centre with MEC Jacob Mamabolo

Summary:
If you live in Gauteng and have an expired driver’s license good luck to you as time is running out and it seems that the backlog will not be cleared any time soon, even as the grace period deadline ends on the 31 August.

You can no longer just walk in to renew your license – you have to make a booking online. But try that and see how far you get. It’s an exercise in lost productivity and you may never strike the lucky moment when slots are opened.

And go online from Akasia to Alberton, across to Carletonville, Sandton, Randburg, Xavier there is only one number of slots available. ZERO. And the only message you get is the following: No test appointments are available for the license code

Recently the Gauteng MEC for Transport Jacob Mamabolo admitted during an unannounced visit to Hammanskraal that it’s unlikely the backlog will be cleared anytime soon and probably not before the deadline. So where does that leave Gauteng motorists – not only exposed on their insurance if they have an accident, but also at the mercy of venal and voracious metro cops – known more for their bribery and corruption than their general concern for traffic flow and motorists well- being. It’s also impossible to hire a car in a different province without a driver’s license.

Mamabola says the online system is not the problem – its extreme inefficiencies and different systems that fall under different levels of government. In fact he describes it as
Multiple problems into which a technology was thrown that simply wasn’t ready for it.

The only option is for national government to extend the deadline once again. But if that doesn’t happen he says – they can only add more testing centres as a solution.
He is adamant that they can’t go back to walk ins – especially with Covid. So what do you do? Sit on the system for hours at a time waiting for the moment it opens and lose days of time, or pay someone to help out.

Further information:
Pensioners are getting up at the crack of dawn and still not getting any joy in Randburg.

On my first attempt on Wednesday last week I arrived at 7.45 on the understanding that it was the day allocated to pensioners. There were two queues on either side of the driveway from the door up to the parking area and when I asked the guard at the door he told me that the allocation of pensioners was finished for the day and advised me to return before 7.00 on Thursday. He said that pensioners could now come Mon - Friday but only 30 would be attended to and the other people waiting were being seen by appointment only made on the on-line booking system which pensioners do not have access to.

I arrived next morning st 5.45 when it was still dark and around six of us formed a queue inside which grew by the time they opened at 7.30 and we were mainly pensioners. They then took the first 15 pensioners only and the remainder were turned away and this also happened again yesterday - max.15 only and the rest were told to come back the next day before 7.00.

I saw pensioners pleading to be seen on the days I was there and many saying that it was not there first time trying to get a renewal .

Script:


Gauteng License Blues Final Script TX Sunday 29th August 2021 FACT CHECKED

Commentary One
Its early on a cold August morning and we are on our way to the Randburg driver’s license testing Centre

Up sound radio

It’s old, degraded and dirty and the only signpost is this one. No cash accepted.
These elderly people are up against a broken system- their only hope to renew a driver’s license, is to arrive in the dark and the cold

Lady in queue
Elderly people have been here since 5 o’clock in the morning and its freezing today!

Commentary Two
Most days just 15 of those over sixty years old, will be allowed in without an appointment- the rest turned away – told to come back on another day

Lady in queue
And knowing that the majority of these people are going to be turned away, I actually feel like crying, to be honest.

Commentary Three
Across the country motorists are caught in a squeeze, facing a deadline that ends a grace period granted for expired licenses. And in Gauteng, the system is dysfunctional.

LINK
The elderly who get an appointment without prebooking, are the only ones, because hundreds of thousands of others are forced to use an online system where getting a slot is as rare an event, as winning an Olympic medal

Commentary four
Nompumelelo Gamede is one of 430 000 Gauteng motorists mired in the backlog. She has lost count of how often she has logged onto the Road traffic management’s site, trying to get a slot.

Nompumelelo I started doing it every day, every day until it was weeks, weeks, months, months, two months. And I'm like, haibo is it me or you know?

Commentary Five
Gamede is a qualified basic life support paramedic. Her job requires a valid driver’s license because at times she drives an ambulance. Without it she cannot work.



Nompumelelo
I literally found a job in the nearby salon. So that's how far I'm willing to go, because there's nothing I can do.

Commentary six
She sometimes wakes with her two month old baby to see if she can get a slot

Nompumelelo
And it kicks you out. So you have to start the process again. And then when you go in, no slots available like literally everything Zero, zero, zero.

Masa try go online now, maybe we'll be lucky.
Nompumulelo OK, so now nothing is available. It is there - everything from Alberton to Heidelburg

Commentary seven
The experience in Randburg is equally frustrating as people in wheelchairs, on oxygen and crutches, join the queue hoping to get through these doors.

Lady 1
I think we need to stand our ground Today
Lady 2
We are going to cling onto every sliver of hope we can find
1, 2, only the applicant no good husband no good wife- six seven eight nine, number 10

Commentary eight
The Gauteng politician that’s accountable is MEC for transport, Jacob Mamabolo. He has taken a lot of flak from journalists, but he prides himself on being transparent and pro-active, and he acknowledges Gauteng has a problem

Jacob Mamabolo
it’s not optimal, it’s not efficient, we are not in denial about that, we are not defensive about it, it’s a reality that people are exposed to on a daily basis.
Masa
MEC motorists find themselves at the mercy of a broken system, that is failing
Mamabolo writes
Masa
So what should we do?
Jacob Mamabolo
We have acknowledged the system has challenges. At the same time we mustn’t completely write off a system that in 6 months has issued 500 000 drivers licenses. The system has challenges, the system is being improved

Commentary nine
Abel Mositsa disagrees. The 300 members of his association of driving schools, can’t get slots to get their clients through the system and some are losing their livelihoods.

Abel
Some of the driving schools are closing, some of them have cars from the bank and the bank are repossessing their cars, it’s a huge challenge

Commentary ten
He says they have pleaded with government, with no answers forthcoming. Now they are planning a protest at the centres next week.

Masa
If you had to rate our MEC Jacob Mamabola and how he is tackling this problem...
Abel
No Mamabolo that one. In March he said he needs three months to resolve this problem. Look from March until now nothing is happening we are still complaining about the very same system.

Commentary eleven
But Mamabolo, with his signature notebook, wants to ensure he has correctly diagnosed the problem on facts alone.

Up sound MEC
To confirm fingerprints...oh beep Okay.

To do that he is making unannounced visits to the testing centres. He invited us to join him in Kagiso.

Mamabolo
Beverley ,where is your boss?
Staff member
The guy in the yellow t-shirt
Mamabolo
is that how you guys dress at work?!

Commentary twelve
Its casual Friday and the manager is taken by surprise. Mamabolo believes outdated technology at the centres is at the root of the problem, not the online system. Manager Bevan Rayners has only two out of 6 stations operational, despite his pleas for new machines.
Bevan
This is a machine that is completely outdated
Jacob
So this is broken?
Bevan
Yes, and they just don’t have the necessary resources or equipment to repair.
Jacob
So this big population, you service with only two machines?
Bevan
Jacob
he bows

LINK
At a time when we can do our tax returns and grocery shopping and everything in between online, the driver’s license system just doesn’t make sense, it’s near impossible to get a slot, and if you do, you can’t pay for it online.

Commentary Thirteen
Book keeper Liesel Grimbeek has two boys. It took her three solid weeks trying every day to book a learners test for her eldest son

Liesel
But when we booked the slot, we got notification that we had to go before his appointment and pay to book the slot or it would lapse

Commentary Fourteen
Her son Zach couldn’t pay with cash, and Grimbeek wasn’t allowed inside. So she gave him him her credit card – and waited in the car. Five long hours passed

Liesel
And when he eventually got to the front of the queue they wouldn't accept the credit card because they said it wasn't in his name as the applicant and then he was told they would do him a favour and accept the payment
Masa
A favour?
Liesel
Yes. And then unfortunately, he did not pass. So now I am trying to find another slot with no success.

Old bloke sings
We’re almost there...

Commentary Fifteen
By late morning, patience in Randburg was wearing thin

Grumpy old lady
So I am giving up, I am going somewhere else, I am just going to find something that works

LINK
Gauteng’s 40 license centres send their slots to the RTMC who then release them onto the computer system, but if corrupt officials are gaming the system, why would they give away the very thing that can earn them thousands of Rands on the side- very rare and clearly valuable slots.



Commentary sixteen
We calculated that at R300 per slot – a corrupt official would only need to process ten a day for ten days to make an extra R30 000 tax free. But Mamabolo says they have appointed a forensic company to investigate all 40 license centres

Jacob Mamabolo
There is a syndicate working with our officials allegedly. They know when the slots are issued they tell their friends and that is how apparently its going, so to all those criminals, it might have become part of their ecosystem daily, but they must know things are no longer the same. There is a big eye watching this space and it’s going to come to them.

Commentary Seventeen
The solution announced on Friday, is two new generation testing centres, mobile buses, online payments and kiosks at Gautrain stations, but none of these will immediately help hapless motorists faced with Gauteng’s metro cops

Jacob
we can assure them if there is no extension, we will be able to work with them to give them slots. Remember in this country we also have a deep routed culture of people not respecting traffic fines, traffic license rules
Masa
No MEC there are far too many people who are trying to be law abiding citizens and those are the people we are talking about here.
Jacob
The law abiding citizens we are going to help them, we will make platforms for them to talk to us, but I am saying we issued many slots but out of the total we issued the number that is important to us is 130 000 have not responded

Commentary eighteen
The MEC appealed to motorists to use the slots that he says are sent to them via SMS
MEC
please respect the slot
Masa
So what are you saying for people who have an invalid driver’s license and they get stopped by an aggressive metro officer who says your license has expired?

MEC
If they still don’t get a slot, I am saying to you definitely minister is going to come and talk to the public and say what is the way forward.

Commentary nineteen
On Friday Minister Fikile Mbalula announced an extension to the end of March 2022.
But Mamabola says solving the backlog must be a partnership between government and motorists



Jacob
Success in turning around the Covid 19 backlog, for us to win it, it will not be the department alone
Masa
I get that but I find it extremely difficult to play my part when I know the problems are derived from old machines, a syndicate that has nothing to do with me. Why must I take some blame in that?
MEC
It’s not blame uh, uh. Those are issues we must solve, that is why I said that everybody has their part to play. but the difficulty I have with the conversation is when we beat the one side of the drum that says that is where all problems are.

Commentary twenty
In the meantime motorists must keep logging onto the Road traffic management site, and hope they win the slot lottery.

Old Boy
All good things come to those who wait ...laughs but the end of our lives are coming too.

THE END 11 00

PROMO ONE

MEC for transport in Gauteng Jacob Mamabolo has been making unannounced visits to driver’s license testing centres, to diagnose why the system isn’t working
Bevan
This is a machine that is completely outdated, they have no equipment to .....they don’t work at all
Jacob
So this is broken
Bevan
Yes, and they don’t have the necessary resources to repair
Jacob
So this big population you service with only two machines – he bows

PROMO TWO
MEC for Transport in Gauteng, Jacob Mamabolo says they are making improvements to the Driver’s license renewal system

Jacob Mamabolo
it’s not optimal, it’s not efficient, we are not in denial about that, we are not defensive about it, it’s a reality that people are exposed to on a daily basis.

PROMO THREE 11 seconds
On Friday the grace period to renew expired drivers licenses was extended, as frustrated motorists queued in the cold for hours, and others battled a dysfunctional online system

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Grace periods to renew Drivers licenses run out at the end of August but Motorists are caught up in a system that doesnt work and politicians who arent offering solutions
metadata.Unique Selling Point: An unexpected site visit to a driving license testing centre with MEC Jacob Mamabolo
metadata.Summary: If you live in Gauteng and have an expired driver’s license good luck to you as time is running out and it seems that the backlog will not be cleared any time soon, even as the grace period deadline ends on the 31 August. You can no longer just walk in to renew your license – you have to make a booking online. But try that and see how far you get. It’s an exercise in lost productivity and you may never strike the lucky moment when slots are opened. And go online from Akasia to Alberton, across to Carletonville, Sandton, Randburg, Xavier there is only one number of slots available. ZERO. And the only message you get is the following: No test appointments are available for the license code Recently the Gauteng MEC for Transport Jacob Mamabolo admitted during an unannounced visit to Hammanskraal that it’s unlikely the backlog will be cleared anytime soon and probably not before the deadline. So where does that leave Gauteng motorists – not only exposed on their insurance if they have an accident, but also at the mercy of venal and voracious metro cops – known more for their bribery and corruption than their general concern for traffic flow and motorists well- being. It’s also impossible to hire a car in a different province without a driver’s license. Mamabola says the online system is not the problem – its extreme inefficiencies and different systems that fall under different levels of government. In fact he describes it as Multiple problems into which a technology was thrown that simply wasn’t ready for it. The only option is for national government to extend the deadline once again. But if that doesn’t happen he says – they can only add more testing centres as a solution. He is adamant that they can’t go back to walk ins – especially with Covid. So what do you do? Sit on the system for hours at a time waiting for the moment it opens and lose days of time, or pay someone to help out.
metadata.Further information: Pensioners are getting up at the crack of dawn and still not getting any joy in Randburg. On my first attempt on Wednesday last week I arrived at 7.45 on the understanding that it was the day allocated to pensioners. There were two queues on either side of the driveway from the door up to the parking area and when I asked the guard at the door he told me that the allocation of pensioners was finished for the day and advised me to return before 7.00 on Thursday. He said that pensioners could now come Mon - Friday but only 30 would be attended to and the other people waiting were being seen by appointment only made on the on-line booking system which pensioners do not have access to. I arrived next morning st 5.45 when it was still dark and around six of us formed a queue inside which grew by the time they opened at 7.30 and we were mainly pensioners. They then took the first 15 pensioners only and the remainder were turned away and this also happened again yesterday - max.15 only and the rest were told to come back the next day before 7.00. I saw pensioners pleading to be seen on the days I was there and many saying that it was not there first time trying to get a renewal .
